cohort: 107 pregnant women with cardiac disease who underwent caesarean section
finding: Parturients with higher NYHA classifications and a history of cardiac surgery or medical treatment were more likely to have general anaesthesia, although newborn weights were lower in the general anaesthesia group, there was no difference in APGAR scores between groups, and the groups were similar with regard to postoperative complications and length of hospital stay
mod_finding: Parturients with cardiac diseases and higher NYHA classifications had higher rates of general anesthesia compared to regional anesthesia for Cesarean section.
